text:
Maya P: I'm doing the handoff — EU region high tail latency on the inference cluster. Seen a steady increase over the last 6m, errors ~0.6% but p95 token latency creeping into SLAs. Primary: Sahil, Secondary: Tess. I'm handing over to night shift (Leon) in 10m.

Sahil: grabbing logs now. initial triage shows KV cache misses spiking on model-v2-quant. Might be warmup / bad caching after the autoscale event.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0421 created by Sahil — severity: P1 (customer-impacting). Pager routed to oncall-sre, oncall-platform.

Tess: thanks — quick checklist from runbook (runbook link below) — verify scaling, check GPU memory pressure, inspect recent routing changes. If tail > 1.2s escalate to SRE Lead.

Maya P: runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/internal/incidents/inference-eu-latency — follow "cold-cache-surge" section. Key pointers inlined below.

Sahil: paste of quick commands I'm running:
```bash
# top hot threads on nodes
redis-cli -h cache-eu-01 latency latest
redwoodctl logs --service=runtime --filter="model:v2-quant" --since=15m
# check batch sizes
redwoodctl metrics query "avg(batch_size) by (node)" --range=15m
```

Leon: I'm the incoming primary in 10m, can you summarize action items I should own during the overlap?

Maya P: - verify dedicated pool hasn't dipped below min-replicas (dedicated-eu)
- enable prefix caching override for heavy prefixes (temp)
- fallback route small fraction (5%) to model-v1-stable (lower latency)
- page Carter if fail-rate > 1% or p95 > 1.5s for 15m
- inform CS (Priya) when we flip fallback routes

Carter: noted. If paged, I will join bridge and rotate to escalation channel; prefer a 3-way bridge with Platform and SRE. If we need infra scaling beyond autoscale limits, I'll request burst quota.

Tess: quick customer-impact note for CS: "Some EU API keys may experience increased latency; we have a fallback ready and will progressively route traffic to stable model. No data loss expected." Priya please confirm wording before I send.

CS: Priya: ok that's fine. Add ETA for mitigation: "expected mitigation within 20-30 minutes depending on scale operations." Will inform the top 10 customers in the affected org list once we enable fallback.

Sahil: logs show three nodes with sustained KV cache miss ratio > 0.35 and 2 nodes reporting nvmem pressure ~85%. I'm going to disable continuous batching for model-v2-quant on those nodes to reduce memory churn. That will increase cost but lower tail.

incident-bot: Pager escalated to: Leon (primary) at +1m; Carter (SRE Lead) at +11m if no ack.

Leon: acked. I'm switching traffic policy to route 5% to v1-stable now. Will monitor for 5m before increasing.

Maya P: before you bump further, run the quick smoke: send 50 test requests with heavy prefix set and check p95. If improvement < 30% revert and page Carter.

Leon: smoke tests: before fallback p95=1.45s; after 5% fallback p95=1.14s — tail improved but still above target 0.9s. Raising fallback to 20% now, will keep monitoring.

Tess: reminder from escalation policy: if customer-impacting latency persists after 20m from first pager, escalate to SRE Exec and Eng Dir. Also capture a few example requests (no PII) and attach to the incident ticket.

Maya P: adding quick excerpt from the "paging rules" section:
- page oncall-sre for P1 immediately
- if throughput throttled or dedicated pool < min for >5m, page oncall-platform
- if mitigation requires quota or cross-team intervention, page SRE Lead (Carter) after 10m
- if significant customer impact (top-10 customers) notify CS Director

Carter: joining bridge in 2m. If nvmem pressure keeps rising we should consider spreading instances across more nodes or temporarily revert quantization for the model on a small subset. That is last resort.

Leon: Carter joined. I'll keep running scaling and watching `model_request_error_rate` and `inference_p95`. Updating incident ticket with all actions.

Sahil: after disabling continuous batching on the hot nodes, error rate dropped to 0.28% and p95 to 0.98s. Looks like the caching churn was the root cause.

Maya P: great — final handoff notes for the night:
- Primary: Leon — own mitigation & customer comms (coord with Priya)
- Secondary: Tess — keep on standby for deeper runtime digging
- Escalation: Carter (SRE Lead) then Eng Dir (if unresolved after 40m)
- Runbook ref: https://runbooks.redwood/internal/incidents/inference-eu-latency#cold-cache-surge
- Postmortem required if P1 > 60m or top-10 customers impacted

CS: Priya: I've sent the initial customer note to the affected list and will update after final stabilization.

Sahil: leaving logs + traces in the ticket. handing off console to Leon. glhf. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0421 status changed to "mitigated" by Leon — monitoring.

Leon: handoff complete. I'll run the post-incident checklist in the morning and loop back on any follow-ups.

Tess: thanks all, great overlap.

Maya P: thanks team, closing my handoff.
